Om Prakash Choudhary And Ors vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 9
November, 2023

Author: Satyavrat Verma
Bench: Satyavrat Verma
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Miscellaneous No.59668 of 2017
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-113 Year-2014 Thana- Piyar District- M
 ======================================================
 1. Om Prakash Choudhary, S/o Ramchandra Choudhary
 2. Ramchandra Choudhary son of Late Mahendra Choudhary
 3. Anita Devi wife of Shri Ramchandra Choudhary All are residents of villa
 Sirshi, P.S. Nanpur, District - Sitamarhi.
 4. Bimlesh Kumar Choudhary @ Bimlesh Kumar son of Shri Devnandan
 Choudhary
 5. Kavita Devi @ Kavita Kumari wife of Shri Bimlesh Kumar Choudhary Both
 residents of village - Bishanpur, P.S. - Katra, District - Muzaffarpur.

sentences.text:
Versus  1. State Of Bihar  2. Priti Kumari wife of Shri Om Prakash Choudhary resident of village - S  P.O. P.S. - Nanpur, District - Sitamarhi.
 ... ... Opposite P  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Amrit Abhijat, Adv
For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Sakir Ahmad, APP  =====

=================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SATYAVRAT VERMA
ORAL ORDER 3 09-11-2023 1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned APP for the State.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners seeks permission to withdraw the quashing application with respect to petitioner No. 1 (Om Prakash Choudhary).

4. Issue notice to the Opposite Party No. 2 by both modes i.e. registered cover with A/D as well as ordinary post for which requisites etc. must be filed on or before 30-11-2023, failing which the present quashing application shall stand rejected without further reference to the Bench.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the meantime, the order dated 25-7-2017 passed by learned ACJM-Vth, Muzaffarpur in connection with Pear PS Case No. 113/2014, whereby cognizance of offences under Sections 420,
406, 498A, 494 and 307 of the IPC read with Sections 3 and 4 of the Dairy Prohibition Act has been taken, shall remain stayed.

7. It is made clear that the order of cognizance has been stayed only against the petitioner nos. 2 to 5.
8.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners are father-in-law, mother-in-law,
brother-in-law (bahnoi) and sister-in-law (nanad) of the OP No. 2.
It is next submitted that whenever any dispute arises in between the husband and the wife, the entire family members are implicated in a mechanical manner with general and omnibus allegations.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioners, at this stage, seeks permission to record the present address of the OP No. 2 in the quashing application.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) SUMIT/-
